explanations: Correct. ordinal() returns the 0-based position. ROJO=0, VERDE=1, AZUL=2.
It prints the number, not the name.

questions.question: Why is it better to use an enum instead of integer constants (public static final int) to represent states?
options: Enums are type-safe — you cannot pass an invalid value
explanations: Memory size is not the main advantage.
Correct. With an int enum, anyone can pass 99 even if the valid states are only 3. With an enum, the compiler validates that you only use defined constants.
== works the same for primitives and enums.
There are significant differences in type safety.

questions.question: Can enums in Java have a public constructor?
options: No, the constructor is always private in an enum
It depends on whether the enum is public or package-private
It can only have a no-argument constructor
explanations: Correct. In Java, the constructor of an enum is always private or package-private. An enum cannot be instantiated from outside.
The access modifier of the enum does not affect the constructor.
It can have parameters, as long as the constructor is private.
